# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Access Control

Shows a warning before sign-in that the system is for authorised users only, and hides the last signed-in user name.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| checkId | `INTUNE-BASE-123-DAccessControl` |
| Source | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.15 and A.8.5, NIS2 art. 21(2)(i) — settings from CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Access_Control.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Access_Control.json) |

> Information security policies often require the first two literally: a general warning at sign-in, and no system or user identification before a successful sign-in. The banner is legally relevant in case of misuse; adapt the text to the organisation's own name before deployment. Hiding the last user name is noticeable for users — they will have to type their full name from now on — so communicate it before you assign it. The three other settings close the sign-in routes that the policy does not name as an approved method: the picture password, the old convenience PIN (not the Windows Hello PIN, which keeps working) and the security questions for local accounts — the latter because a password reset should require identity verification, and security questions bypass exactly that.
